tower.meta.v1.Condition.description: Condition is one observed aspect of an object's state, such as "Ready".

observedGeneration.description: The generation this condition was computed from.

reason.description: CamelCase machine-readable cause of the last transition.

status.description: ConditionStatus is the state of a condition.

tower.meta.v1.ObjectMeta.description: ObjectMeta is the metadata every resource carries. Users set name, project, labels and annotations; everything else is owned by the system. See docs/decisions/apply-semantics.md.

annotations.description: Keys under a *.tower.hangarlab.cloud/ prefix are reserved for the system.

deleteTime.description: Set when deletion was requested and finalizers are still pending.

generation.description: Incremented on every change to spec.

labels.description: Keys under a *.tower.hangarlab.cloud/ prefix are reserved for the system.

name.description: DNS-1123 label, unique within the project (or the platform, for global kinds). An Invitation's is an email instead.

resourceVersion.description: Store revision of the last write to this object.

tower.meta.v1.OwnerReference.description: OwnerReference points at the object that owns this one. An owner is in the same project, a global object, or, for a global object, one in the project the reference names; when it is deleted, its dependents are garbage collected.

controller.description: The owner is the controller responsible for this object.

project.description: The owner's project, when the owner is project-scoped and this object is global, as a RoleBinding owned by the ServiceToken it names. Empty otherwise.

tower.secrets.v1alpha1.SealedData.description: SealedData is a secret's data encrypted under a key of its own, which is itself encrypted under tower's key-encryption key.

contentHmac.description: An HMAC of the data, as status.content_hmac shows it.

kekId.description: Names the key-encryption key that wrapped wrapped_key.

nonce.description: The data, encrypted under the secret's own key.

wrappedKey.description: The secret's own key, encrypted under the key-encryption key.

tower.secrets.v1alpha1.SecretSpec.description: SecretSpec is what the secret holds.

data.description: The values, by key, at most 64 KiB in all. Write-only: every apply carries them, and every answer leaves them out. A registry-auth secret holds one key, ".dockerconfigjson", in the Docker config format, as docker login writes it. An opaque secret's keys are environment variable names.

sealed.description: What the apiserver stores of data, encrypted. It is the apiserver's alone: an apply that sets it is refused, and no answer holds it.

type.description:
SecretType says what a secret holds and how its data is checked.

- SECRET_TYPE_REGISTRY_AUTH: A container registry login, in the Docker config format.
- SECRET_TYPE_OPAQUE: Values by environment variable name, as a privileged profile's credentials or a blueprint's required secrets.

tower.secrets.v1alpha1.SecretStatus.description: SecretStatus is what can be said of a secret without its values.

contentHmac.description: A keyed hash of the data, which changes when the data does; it cannot be checked against a guess without tower's key.

registries.description: The registries a registry-auth secret holds a login for, by host.

description: Secret holds credentials for tower to use on a project's behalf: a privileged profile's credentials, what a blueprint needs, a registry login. Its values are write-only: apply sets them, and no answer, event, log line or error ever holds them again. They are stored encrypted, and tower hands them only to the one environment that uses them, never into a spec of a lower layer. See docs/decisions/secrets.md.
title: Secret
